key_insight: A continuous-variable flag oscillator can capture ancilla decay-induced continuous errors during bosonic gates and allow feedback that removes them up to a code stabilizer.
engineering_relevance: This offers a hardware-compatible way to protect bosonic quantum memories and gates in platforms like superconducting circuits and trapped ions without adding fundamentally new control primitives.
method: Couple an auxiliary oscillator to the ancilla so its phase-space state encodes the induced error.
Measure the flag with heterodyne detection after the gate to estimate the continuous error.
Apply feedback correction to undo the error, using the same dispersive couplings, displacements, and rotations already used for the gate.
evidence_signal: Simulations with realistic circuit-QED parameters report more than three orders of magnitude fewer logical errors for a four-component cat-code parity measurement and near-noiseless-ancilla lifetime for a finite-energy GKP code.
watch_item: Performance depends on accurate flag readout and feedback timing, and the protection guarantees differ by gate type, with some requiring more flags or only achieving first-order correction.
paper_title: Protecting bosonic codes from ancilla-induced errors with continuous-variable flags
